title: The roadmap gets re-weighed as a whole, and notes stay short
why: Your question, Oct 26: are we rewriting notes instead of appending, and re-weighing the order instead of putting each new item at the front? Audit, Oct 26 at roadmap 9517045: mostly not.
note:
Audit, Oct 26 at roadmap 9517045 (reports/roadmap-upkeep-audit.md in project files): 85 of 135 note edits were appends; no existing step was ever re-ordered; new steps landed at the top; the whole review never ran, because its trigger (a phase change) never fired. Your ruling, Oct 26 ('agreed, let's implement this'): the thread 'Triage the roadmap' is the gatekeeper. Only it creates, merges, orders and closes steps; other threads send it each item with your message attached and still rewrite notes on their own steps. The coordinator put the rule in the project instructions. Built Oct 26: build.py prints an upkeep list on each build. Against context rot: triage re-reads the branch before each placement, hands off at about 40 exchanges, a phase change or a slip (handoffs/triage-<date>.md), and treats a growing upkeep list as a slip. Your word, Oct 26: the backlog cleanup runs in its own thread, 'Clean up the roadmap backlog'; triage re-weighs the whole order when it reports done. Placed ahead of c53 (triage, Oct 26): it governs how every later step is filed, and it builds nothing in claude-settings main.
Ruling, Oct 26 (shiv): any step that needs your answer is deferred for now; work that needs none runs first, in priority order, and the build advisor dispatches no deferred step.
- Oct 26 (shiv): the local liaison is exempt from the 40-message and 8-brief hand-off limits while it holds a Remote Control session on the Mac; the slip trigger still applies. Oct 26: the project caps thread-to-thread sends at 60 an hour (topic t16, how to use this project); standing threads batch routine notes and retry a refused send.
